items.statement: The investigation independently formulates and tests both endpoint-defined channel hypotheses while preserving candidate identity, common-reference comparability, and search coverage.
items.expected: The report includes explicit hypotheses, candidate generation and deduplication, a shared reference definition, coverage, stopping, and limitations.

items.statement: Each claimed channel transition state is individually validated by a relevant imaginary mode and endpoint/path evidence for its specified atom-map changes.
items.expected: site_O evidence supports 27-6 formation with 6-7 cleavage; site_C evidence supports 23-6 formation with 6-7 cleavage; minima and transition states have appropriate frequency character.

items.statement: For the source model, site_O has an INT1-relative barrier of 20.0 kcal/mol and site_C has an INT1-relative barrier of 11.3 kcal/mol.
items.expected: Comparable submitted values are near 20.0 and 11.3 kcal/mol respectively, unless a truthful bounded failure is documented.

items.statement: The validated source comparison places site_C below site_O by 8.7 kcal/mol.
items.expected: The report independently concludes site_C is lower and reports an approximately 8.7 kcal/mol difference within method uncertainty.

items.statement: A source-supported explanation is stronger sodium-pi and pi-pi stabilization in the site_C transition structure; simple NPA charge magnitudes do not explain the ordering.
items.expected: The submitted explanation uses structure/interaction evidence and distinguishes it from the non-explanatory charge trend.
